title: 3 · Schedules & Serializability (Unit 3)
learn:
Schedule

A schedule is the chronological ordering of the operations of several transactions. A serial schedule never interleaves transactions, so it is always consistent, but it limits concurrency and wastes CPU. A complete schedule ends every transaction with commit or abort.

Recoverability

Recoverable: if Tj reads data written by Ti, Ti must commit before Tj. Non-recoverable: Tj reads Ti's dirty value and commits first; if Ti then fails, Tj cannot be rolled back. Cascading rollback: one failure forces dependent transactions to abort. Cascadeless: a transaction reads a value only after the writer commits. Strict: no read or overwrite until the writer commits or aborts. Every strict schedule is recoverable and cascadeless.

Conflict serializability

Conflicting pairs on the same item by different transactions: R-W, W-R, W-W. Draw a precedence graph (edge Ti → Tj if Ti's conflicting operation comes first). A schedule is conflict serializable if and only if the graph has no cycle.

Example: S: R1(x) R2(x) W1(x) R1(y) W2(x) W1(y). R2(x) before W1(x) gives 2→1; R1(x) before W2(x) gives 1→2. Cycle, so not conflict serializable.

View serializability

A schedule is view serializable if it is view equivalent to a serial schedule: same initial reads, same update (write-read) sources and same final writes. Every conflict-serializable schedule is view serializable, but not the other way round.

quiz.q: A schedule is conflict serializable if and only if its precedence graph is?
Which pair is NOT a conflict?
In a recoverable schedule, if Tj reads from Ti, then?
Which schedule type forbids reading OR overwriting uncommitted data?

quiz.why: But view serializable does not imply conflict serializable.

quiz.q: Edges 1→2 and 2→1 appear in the graph. The schedule is?

lab.task: Test S: R1(A) W1(A) R2(A) W2(A) R1(B) W1(B). Draw the edges and decide.
lab.solution: W1(A) before R2(A) and W2(A) gives 1→2. R2(A)/W2(A) vs later R1(B)/W1(B) touch different items. Only edge 1→2, no cycle: conflict serializable (equivalent to T1 then T2).
